idea-plugin.name: API Security Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Security checks for Java and Kotlin APIs, run inside the IDE's own highlighting pass: hardcoded secrets, leaked tokens in config files, plaintext HTTP, trust-all TLS and OWASP API Top 10 risks. 100% local: no account, no cloud scan, no network calls.

Free

  • Hardcoded secrets in Java and Kotlin: AWS keys, GitHub and Slack tokens, Stripe keys, JWTs and PEM private keys, plus a name-and-entropy check for generic secrets.
  • Leaked tokens in config files (JSON, YAML, .properties, .env), including MCP server configs such as mcp.json and claude_desktop_config.json: 20+ fixed formats, among them OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, GitHub, GitLab, npm, PyPI, Stripe and AWS. Template files and ${VAR} references are skipped.
  • Plaintext HTTP URLs to non-local hosts.
  • TLS trust managers that accept every certificate (CWE-295), in Java and Kotlin.
  • OWASP API Security Top 10: Excessive Data Exposure and Mass Assignment in Java REST endpoints.
  • OpenAPI specs (YAML): an empty top-level security requirement, and wildcard CORS combined with credentials.

Every rule can be turned off individually in Settings.

API Security Companion Pro (paid, with a free trial)

  • Kotlin support for Excessive Data Exposure and Mass Assignment, including Kotlin code that uses Java entities.
  • Broken Object Level Authorization (OWASP API1): endpoints that take an object ID with no visible ownership check, reported as potential issues to review.
  • Unrestricted Resource Consumption (OWASP API4): page-size and limit parameters with no upper bound.
  • Credential-named keys in config files (client_secret, DB_PASSWORD, Authorization: Bearer ...) with a high-entropy value.
  • Team rules: commit a .gaphunter-security-rules file, and every rule it lists stays on for each licensed team member, even if someone turns it off locally.
  • On-device ML filter, off by default: fewer false positives on generic high-entropy matches. It never touches recognized formats such as AWS keys or JWTs.
